note: Repo-intake language classification, added on claude/repo-intake-adapter (repo-intake track). `adapters/repo_adapter.py` dispatches by looking a file's name up in this table — never an `if ext == ... ` chain — the same plug-in shape seed/CHARTS.json gives charts. `class` is one of chart-worthy (a replayable warrant floor exists at v0 -- elaboration, or AST + a runnable test suite -- so the file is routed straight to its chart's Document); reference-tier (no replayable floor at v0; HELD by the adapter -- counted and hashed, but no Document is built, since ingesting it as English claims about the code is future work, not this adapter's job); shelf (binary / generated / no parse -- hashed for the report, never read as text). `match` is `filename` (exact, tried first) or `extension` (case-insensitive, tried second); first match wins. Adding a new chart-worthy language later is a row here plus the chart's own manifest row in seed/CHARTS.json -- no adapter code changes.

rules.reason: machine-generated dependency lockfile; no authored claim to read
AST gives a deterministic structural segmenter; the repo's own unittest suite, actually run, gives a replayable CI_RECEIPT-tier floor (adapters/python_corpus.py)
kernel elaboration under a pinned toolchain is a replayable KERNEL-tier floor (adapters/lean_corpus.py); existing chart, reused, not duplicated

prose about code; no compiler/kernel/test check exists for an English claim at v0 -- would be ingested later only as English claims about the code, via the existing english chart, at EXTRACTION tier at best
`go build`/`go test` could in principle supply a CI_RECEIPT-analogous floor the way Python's unittest run does, but that adapter is not built at v0 -- held rather than guessed at
no deterministic, dependency-free replayable check wired at v0 (a JS test runner is a third-party toolchain, not stdlib)
same as .js; a type-checker is a real floor candidate for a later chart, not built at v0
shell is side-effecting; running it to check a claim is not a parse and is unsafe to do for grounding, so no replayable floor at v0
declarative config data, not a truth-apt claim; a schema check could floor it later but none is wired
declarative config/data; same reasoning as .yml (lockfiles are overridden above by filename)
declarative config data; same reasoning as .yml

default.reason: unregistered extension; no manifest rule -- default is shelf (no parse), not a silent guess
